About red scaly patches on my elbows, maybe a three out of ten on a bad day. Yes, cold weather and stress. That makes it worse.\nSEG0010 person_1 (PATIENT) 88.49-97.43s: Stiff fingers in the morning was there, you know, but it's gone away on its own.\nSEG0011 person_2 (DOCTOR) 99.38-103.54s: Okay, did you get fever, eye redness or weeping?\nSEG0012 person_1 (PATIENT) 104.98-109.09s: No, no fever, eye redness or weeping.\nSEG0013 person_2 (DOCTOR) 110.04-115.40s: Did you get joint swelling or sore throat before it started?\nSEG0014 person_1 (PATIENT) 116.87-119.51s: No, I'd have mentioned it.\nSEG0015 person_2 (DOCTOR) 125.01-128.92s: Any pins and needles or loss of strength anywhere?\nSEG0016 person_1 (PATIENT) 130.12-132.42s: No, that's all normal.\nSEG0017 person_2 (DOCTOR) 133.14-134.41s: Any previous surgeries?\nSEG0018 person_1 (PATIENT) 135.50-137.10s: No operations, no.\nSEG0019 person_2 (DOCTOR) 138.46-140.66s: Anything special about your diet?\nSEG0020 person_1 (PATIENT) 142.30-145.95s: I try to avoid too much sugar.\nSEG0021 person_2 (DOCTOR) 151.35-153.83s: Okay, do you exercise at all?\nSEG0022 person_1 (PATIENT) 154.54-161.10s: I go to the gym a couple of times a week.\nSEG0023 person_2 (DOCTOR) 169.39-173.31s: Any long-term health problems I should know about?\nSEG0024 person_1 (PATIENT) 178.30-188.46s: So, I have diabetes. Sorry, I know I'm rambling a bit. I have high blood pressure, for about a year.\nSEG0025 person_2 (DOCTOR) 190.03-192.89s: Any allergies I should know about?\nSEG0026 person_1 (PATIENT) 193.46-200.63s: Yes, aspirin, it gives me a rash. Yes, I'm allergic to sulfa drugs.\nSEG0027 person_2 (DOCTOR) 211.02-215.43s: Any medication at the moment, including things from the pharmacy?\nSEG0028 person_1 (PATIENT) 217.15-221.01s: It's amlodipine, 5 milligrams, once a day.\nSEG0029 person_3 (CAREGIVER) 221.80-231.84s: Uh, it's meant to be once a day, though I don't see she take it every time.\nSEG0030 person_2 (DOCTOR) 250.44-252.98s: Let me check your vitals now.\nSEG0031 person_2 (DOCTOR) 264.90-267.43s: Okay, give me a moment...\nSEG0032 person_2 (DOCTOR) 282.33-291.02s: Okay: temp 36.4 degrees, pulse is 70 beats a minute, pressure 122 over 72, oxygen saturation is 98 percent.\nSEG0033 person_2 (DOCTOR) 293.07-296.49s: Let me examine, it won't take long.\nSEG0034 person_2 (DOCTOR) 297.69-300.09s: Hold that position for me.\nSEG0035 person_2 (DOCTOR) 315.13-317.95s: A few small pits in the fingernails.\nSEG0036 person_2 (DOCTOR) 319.04-320.92s: Let me press here.\nSEG0037 person_2 (DOCTOR) 330.75-334.27s: Well-defined thick silvery plaques over both elbows and knees.\nSEG0038 person_2 (DOCTOR) 340.22-353.11s: That's fine, sit up. Taking everything into account, this looks most like plaque psoriasis. I'd also keep eczema in mind. A little sunlight helps psoriasis, but avoid sunburn. Moisturise often.\nSEG0039 person_2 (DOCTOR) 353.69-359.74s: Right. We'll catch up in six weeks. Right, ask me anything before you go.\nSEG0040 person_1 (PATIENT) 361.29-367.20s: I, I think that's clear. Thank you for being so thorough.",
